title: Distinct Subsequences
description:
Given two strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s which equal t.

A subsequence of a string is a new string formed from the original string by deleting some (possibly zero) of the characters without disturbing the relative positions of the remaining characters. For example, "ACE" is a subsequence of "ABCDE" while "AEC" is not.

The answer fits within a 32-bit signed integer.

examples.explanation: There are 3 ways to generate "rabbit" from "rabbbit" by deleting one of the three 'b' characters.
There are 5 ways to generate "bag" from "babgbag" by choosing different combinations of the matching characters.

constraints: s and t consist of English letters.
The answer is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
approach: Let dp[j] count the distinct ways to form the first j characters of t using the source characters seen so far. Start with dp[0] = 1 because the empty target is always matched exactly once. For each character of s, iterate j from high to low: when the source character equals t[j-1], add dp[j-1] to dp[j]. Iterating backward ensures dp[j-1] still reflects counts before the current source character, so a single source character is never reused within one update. The final answer is dp[len(t)]. For source length m and target length n, time is O(mn) and space is O(n).
